steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: A semiconductor diode allows current to flow in one direction only; it has a forward voltage drop of about 0.7 V for silicon. | Key Fact: An LED (light-emitting diode) emits light when forward biased; it requires a series resistor to limit current. | Key Fact: A bipolar junction transistor (BJT) has three terminals: base, collector and emitter. | Key Fact: An NPN transistor switches on when the base-emitter voltage exceeds ~0.7 V, allowing collector current to flow.
